title: FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 03 (Prose & Novel Comprehensive)
subject: english-12

questions.question: What modern method of food preservation preserves flavor and vitamins while preventing bacterial decay through rapid temperature reduction?

options.A: Excessive pickling with vinegar

questions.explanation: Quick-freezing stops bacterial enzymatic action while preserving texture, nutritional vitamins, and fresh flavor in vegetables and meats.

questions.question: In 'The Dying Sun', why did the mountain raised on the sun by the wandering star burst into fragments?

options.A: Because the sun's internal pressure exceeded its outer crust threshold.
options.B: Because the star came closer and its gravitational pull exceeded the sun's cohesive strength, tearing the tidal crest off.
options.C: Due to a direct physical collision between the two celestial bodies.
options.D: Because of rapid thermal contraction as the sun cooled down.

questions.explanation: As the wandering star drew nearer, the tidal wave rose so high that its summit detached under overwhelming gravitational attraction, hurling pieces into orbit.

questions.question: What terror seized the author while carrying his heavy sack along the Chelsea embankment at night?

options.A: Fear that a passing policeman would suspect him of carrying a murdered baby or stolen silverware
options.B: Fear that thieves would steal his precious poetry volumes
options.C: Fear that the sack would tear and books would fall into a sewer
options.D: Fear of ghosts from the London cemeteries

questions.explanation: A policeman loomed up in the fog, and Squire panicked that his nervous pacing and suspicious sack would look like the disposal of a corpse.

questions.question: What witty reply did the chemist give Jerome when handed the doctor's prescription?

options.A: 'That will cost twenty guineas, sir.'
options.B: 'I am a chemist, sir, not a family hotel and a livery stable combined.'
options.C: 'This medicine is strictly out of stock.'

questions.explanation: Since the prescription contained beefsteak and lodging instructions rather than chemical compounds, the chemist politely declined.

questions.question: What is the administrative unit of agricultural production in Maoist China known as?

options.A: The People's Commune (split into Production Brigades and Production Teams)

questions.explanation: Communes organized rural labor democratically, coordinating farming, schooling, irrigation, and local militia.

questions.question: In Santini's description of Chinese cities, what striking absence distinguishes them from Western metropolises?

options.A: An absence of commercial advertising, neon signs, luxury private cars, and drug epidemics
options.B: An absence of streets and sidewalks
options.C: A complete lack of trees and parks

questions.explanation: Chinese cities were characterized by sea of bicycles, simple clothing, and an absence of corporate billboards, glamour, and street vice.

questions.question: When Christopher and his companions ran out of drinking water in the blistering wasteland, what desperate measure saved their lives?

options.A: Digging deep artesian wells by hand in two minutes
options.B: Draining the rusty, oily, scalding water from the truck's engine radiator and filtering it through a cloth to drink
options.D: Summoning a helicopter via satellite phone

questions.explanation: They drained foul, oily boiling water from the radiator, allowing it to cool and settle before desperately drinking it to avoid death by dehydration.

questions.question: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: 'Churchill's *broad-minded* headmaster recognized his potential.'

options.A: Compound adjective

questions.explanation: 'Broad-minded' is a hyphenated compound adjective modifying the noun 'headmaster'.

questions.question: Who was the first human patient successfully treated by Pasteur for rabies (hydrophobia) in July 1885?

options.A: Joseph Meister, a nine-year-old Alsatian boy severely bitten by a mad dog
options.B: A French shepherd named Jean-Baptiste Jupille

questions.explanation: Little Joseph Meister had fourteen deep wounds from a rabid dog; Pasteur's series of 13 attenuated spinal cord injections prevented rabies and saved his life.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the medical term 'attenuation' in immunology?

options.A: Weakening the virulence of a pathogen so it stimulates immunity without causing disease

questions.explanation: 'Attenuation' is the reduction of virulence in a microbe, enabling its use as a safe, protective vaccine.

questions.question: In Castle's essay, how did Mustafa Kemal handle economic development in the new republic?

options.A: By selling all natural resources to British cartels
options.B: Through state-directed industrialization (Five-Year Plans), building railways, iron mills, textile factories, and a modern banking network without foreign debt
options.D: By shutting down agriculture to focus exclusively on tourism

questions.explanation: Under the principle of Étatisme (Statism), Turkey built sovereign heavy industries, ports, and national railways financed by domestic capital.

questions.question: Identify the type of conditional sentence: 'If Mustafa Kemal had not rallied the Anatolian people, Turkey would have been carved up among European powers.'

options.A: Zero Conditional
options.D: Third Conditional (Hypothetical past situation with past result)

questions.explanation: 'Had + past participle' in the if-clause followed by 'would have + past participle' in the main clause defines the Third Conditional.

questions.question: Before meeting Katherine, how was Chips regarded by his colleagues at Brookfield?

options.A: As a brilliant future Prime Minister
options.B: As a quiet, respectable, dry, and somewhat uninspiring middle-aged classical master who had reached his peak

questions.explanation: He was a conventional, hardworking teacher of modest academic attainments who seemed destined to become a dull, forgotten fixture.

questions.question: What was Brookfield's status among English public schools?

options.A: An elite institution equal to Eton and Harrow
options.B: A reputable, respectable second-rank school that had weathered historical ups and downs since the reign of Queen Elizabeth
options.D: A military academy for infantry cadets

questions.explanation: Brookfield was not an aristocratic giant like Eton, but a solid school that produced judges, civil servants, clergy, and country squires.

questions.question: Who succeeded Ralston as Headmaster of Brookfield in 1911?

options.A: Mr. Chatteris, a charming, brilliant, and hardworking man of thirty-four

questions.explanation: Chatteris took over: he was diplomatic, modern, respectful of Chips, and suffered from diabetic health problems.

questions.question: What did Chips do immediately after moving into Mrs. Wickett's house across the road?

options.A: He continued to invite new boys and masters to his tea-table, attended chapel and school matches, and remained the elder statesman of Brookfield.
options.B: He cut all ties with the school.
options.D: He spent all his savings on racehorses.

questions.explanation: Retirement merely changed his address by fifty yards; he remained an active, welcoming grandfather figure to the entire school.

questions.question: In what year did Mr. Chips pass away?

options.A: November 1933, at the age of eighty-five

questions.explanation: Chips died peacefully in November 1933, having lived eighty-five rich, honorable, and beloved years.

questions.question: What was the significance of Linford's visit to Chips?

options.A: It completed the circle of his life: his final living conversation was with a lonely young schoolboy who needed comfort and warmth.

questions.explanation: Hilton poignantly bookends Chips' career with an innocent schoolboy, proving that Chips' ministry of love continued to his final breath.

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect form of: The teacher said to the boys, 'Do not make a noise.'

options.A: The teacher forbade the boys to make a noise.
options.B: The teacher forbade the boys not to make a noise.
options.C: The teacher said to the boys that they should not make noise.
options.D: The teacher told the boys to not make a noise.

questions.explanation: The verb 'forbade' already contains a negative meaning, so adding 'not' would create an erroneous double negative.

questions.question: What does the idiom 'to take to task' mean?

options.A: To assign school homework
options.B: To reprimand, scold, or severely criticize someone for a blunder

questions.explanation: 'Taking someone to task' means rebuking or reprimanding them sternly for wrongdoing.
